what_it_is.prose: The Zorawar Light Tank is a 25-tonne Indian light tank designed by the Combat Vehicles Research & Development Establishment (CVRDE, a DRDO laboratory) and integrated by Larsen & Toubro (L&T) as the lead systems integrator under the Indian Army's Make-I category (government-funded prototype development). The tank is purpose-built for high-altitude warfare in Eastern Ladakh and is named after General Zorawar Singh, the 19th-century Dogra general who campaigned in the Himalayas. The Zorawar is powered by a Cummins VTA903E-T760 760 hp diesel engine (USA) — selected after the originally-planned MTU 8V199 engine (Rolls-Royce Germany) was blocked by German export controls in 2022-23. The power-to-weight ratio is 30-40 hp/tonne, giving the tank exceptional mobility in mountainous terrain. The main armament is a Cockerill 105 mm HP rifled gun in a John Cockerill 3105 turret (Belgium), supplemented by a 7.62 mm BEL Remote Controlled Weapon Station and twin side-mounted launchers for the Nag Mk2 Anti-Tank Guided Missile. The hunter-killer EO/IR suite comprises two Safran Paseo sights (France) with thermal imager and laser range finder. The transmission is a RENK America HMPT-800 (USA/Germany), the same unit used on the US Army's Armored Multi-Purpose Vehicle (AMPV). Armour is STANAG 4569 Level 4 frontal / Level 2 sides, with Level 6/5B under development by the Defence Metallurgical Research Laboratory (DMRL). The Indian Army's initial order was for 59 tanks (one regiment) placed in April 2023 with L&T as development-cum-production partner; the total programme of record is 354 tanks (59 + 295 via Make-I competitive bidding), at approximately ₹70 crore per tank and a total programme value of approximately ₹17,500 crore. The second batch of 295 tanks is open to competitive bidding — Bharat Forge and Armoured Vehicles Nigam (AVNL) are both developing competitors under the Futuristic Light Tank programme. Army Chief General Upendra Dwivedi stated on 4 June 2026 that the Zorawar will be inducted in 2028-29, after fixes from developmental trials are incorporated. MSMEs in Vadodara, Rajkot, and Surat contributed gear mechanisms, rubber foundry, and cooling system components.

faq.question: Why was the Zorawar engine switched from MTU to Cummins?
faq.answer: The Zorawar was originally planned to use the MTU 8V199 engine from Rolls-Royce Germany. However, German export controls blocked the supply in 2022-23, forcing L&T to switch to the Cummins VTA903E-T760 (760 hp diesel) sourced directly from the USA. The Cummins engine provides 30-40 hp/tonne power-to-weight ratio, giving the tank exceptional mobility in high-altitude terrain. The episode highlights the strategic risk of European export-control chokepoints in Indian defence programmes.

faq.question: When will the Zorawar enter service?
faq.answer: Army Chief General Upendra Dwivedi stated on 4 June 2026 that the Zorawar will be inducted in 2028-29, after fixes from developmental trials are incorporated. The initial order is for 59 tanks (one regiment) placed with L&T in April 2023. The total programme of record is 354 tanks at approximately ₹17,500 crore.

faq.question: Why is the Zorawar named after General Zorawar Singh?
faq.answer: The Zorawar Light Tank is named after General Zorawar Singh (1786-1841), the 19th-century Dogra general who campaigned extensively in the Himalayas and Tibet under Maharaja Gulab Singh of Jammu. The name reflects the tank's intended role in high-altitude warfare in Eastern Ladakh and along the Line of Actual Control with China — terrain similar to where General Zorawar Singh operated. The naming follows the Indian tradition of invoking military historical figures for indigenous defence platforms (cf. Tejas, Arjun, Dhruv, Prachand).
